forms.why_en: Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Adds -n for 'I': tarvita becomes tarvitsen. Speech says tarviin.
As the thing you need, sairauslomatodistus takes -n: sairauslomatodistuksen.
The illative plural of työ: töihin, 'to work, for work'. People say it the same way.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.
Kauan, long, with -ko to ask. Speech says -ks: kauanks.
Speech shortens sinä to sä. Books write sinä.
Speech drops the l and stretches the vowel: olet becomes oot. Books write olet. From olla, to be.
From olla, to be. After 'olet' this form says 'have been'. Speech drops the last t: ollu.
Speech turns -eä into -ee: kipeä becomes kipee.
Maanantai with -sta for 'from': maanantaista. Speech drops the last vowel: maanantaist.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: past tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.lemma_meaning_en: to visit, to go, to be OK
forms.why_en: Adds -i for the past, -t for 'you' and -kö to ask: kävitkö. Speech drops -kö: kävit sä.
Adds -llä for 'at': lääkäri becomes lääkärillä.
Joo is the everyday spoken yes. Books write kyllä.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Adds -n for 'I': tulostaa becomes tulostan.
Se with -n when the whole thing is the object: kirjoittaa sen.
Sinä with -lle for 'to, for'. Speech shortens it to sulle.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech says vaan. Books write vain.
Kiitti is the everyday spoken thanks. Books write kiitos.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 1st person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.lemma_meaning_en: to get, to be allowed to
forms.why_en: Saada adds -n for 'I' and -ko to ask: saanko. Speech says saanks.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Adds -in for 'into': sähköposti becomes sähköpostiin.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Löytyä 'to be found' doubles its last vowel for 'it': löytyy.
OmaKanta with -sta for 'from' or 'in it': Omakannasta. The t softens to n. Speech drops the last vowel.
